name: Tapo T315 (UK)

radios.note: The UK page says it works only in a sub-1 GHz band to the Tapo Hub, which is not in our radio list.

matter.note: The sensor itself isn't Matter-certified in any source we found; Tapo Hubs can bridge it to Matter.

apple_home.note: TP-Link's UK Matter FAQ names the T315 among sub-1 GHz devices a Tapo Hub can add to another ecosystem through its Matter Bridge, and names Apple TV and the Home app as Matter controllers.

google_home.note: Through the Tapo Hub's Matter Bridge; the same FAQ names Google Nest Hub as a Matter controller.

alexa.note: Through the Tapo Hub's Matter Bridge; the same FAQ names an Echo as a Matter controller.

smartthings.note: TP-Link's Matter FAQ doesn't name SmartThings as a controller for bridged devices.

home_assistant.note: No official source confirms it; Home Assistant could use the hub's Matter bridge but we couldn't cite it.

hubRequired.note: The UK page says the Tapo Hub is required for smart features and for third-party platforms.

localControl.note: Not confirmed from an official source.

power.note: Up to 2 years in lab conditions per Tapo.

summary: Temperature and humidity readings on a 2.7-inch e-ink screen: that is the Tapo T315 (UK). It reaches Apple Home, Google Home and Alexa only through a Tapo Hub's Matter Bridge, and the hub is required for its smart features. The sensor links to the hub over a sub-1 GHz band, not Wi-Fi, and runs on 2 AAA batteries that Tapo rates at up to 2 years.
caveats: Needs a Tapo Hub; the sensor doesn't join Wi-Fi or Matter itself.
SmartThings and Home Assistant support isn't confirmed by TP-Link.
Matter bridging needs a Tapo Hub on current firmware; TP-Link's FAQ doesn't list which hub models qualify for this sensor.
